eventMetadata.context_description: The Orlando Magic grabbed a stunning 1-0 series lead over the top-seeded Detroit Pistons with a 112-101 road upset in Game 1 on April 19, fueled by Paolo Banchero's 23 points, Franz Wagner's clutch fourth-quarter scoring, and stifling defense that held Detroit to 40.3% shooting despite Cade Cunningham's 39-point effort. This victory extended the Pistons' NBA-longest home playoff losing streak, shifting trader sentiment toward Orlando's momentum as the No. 8 seed faces Game 2 on April 22 at Little Caesars Arena. Key factors include Magic forward Jonathan Isaac ruled out with a left knee sprain, while Detroit reports a clean injury slate; Pistons' regular-season dominance (60-22 record) and home-court edge loom large for a bounce-back, with Game 3 shifting to Orlando on April 25 amid playoff implications for both young cores.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Lakers hold a commanding 2-0 series lead over the Rockets in their Western Conference first-round playoff matchup after home wins of 107-98 in Game 1 and 101-94 in Game 2, fueled by LeBron James' 28-point outings and Luke Kennard's 27-point explosion in the opener amid absences of Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves due to injuries. Houston, the No. 5 seed at 52-30, has been plagued by Steven Adams and Fred VanVleet sidelined, plus Kevin Durant's questionable knee status limiting his Game 2 efficiency despite a return. Game 3 shifts to Houston for Rockets' home-court edge and desperation to avoid an 0-3 deficit, with trader focus on updated injury reports, LeBron's playoff form at age 41, and momentum swings in this injury-riddled clash between evenly matched 52- and 53-win squads.

President Trump extended the fragile two-week ceasefire indefinitely on April 21 at Pakistan's request, but tensions escalated with Iran's seizure of ships in the Strait of Hormuz and mutual threats of resumed hostilities. The US naval blockade persists, blocking Iranian oil exports, while Tehran demands its end alongside sanctions relief. Core sticking points—Iran's uranium enrichment, proxy militias, and Hormuz access—underscore deep divides, with a second round of mediated talks uncertain but potentially imminent, tempering trader optimism for a permanent deal.

title: US x Iran ceasefire extended by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran announced on April 7, 2026, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed extension to the halt in direct military engagement between the United States and Iran, by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Both extensions of the April 7 ceasefire and new agreements scheduled to take effect before or at the initial agreement's scheduled end will be considered extensions of the ceasefire agreement, provided there is no period during which no ceasefire is in effect.

If a qualifying agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire extension ultimately takes effect. 

An extension of the ceasefire agreement requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another for longer than the initially agreed two-week period, or for an official extension of the ceasefire agreement in place to be otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation, or unilateral pause in hostilities without a confirmed agreement on a qualifying extension will not qualify. Similarly, newly agreed-upon humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not qualify.

A newly agreed-upon broader peace deal will qualify if it includes a qualifying extension of the ceasefire agreement/halt in military hostilities. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures, but do not explicitly commit to extending the ceasefire, will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire extension agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Oklahoma City Thunder's commanding 119-84 Game 1 rout of the Phoenix Suns in their Western Conference first-round NBA playoffs series underscores the reigning champions' depth and defensive prowess, holding Phoenix to 35% shooting and 19 turnovers while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 25 points. With OKC's pristine injury report—only rookie Thomas Sorber (torn ACL) sidelined—the 64-18 top seed enjoys home-court edge (34-7 at Paycom Center) heading into Game 2 on April 22. Suns (45-37, No. 7 seed), struggling offensively despite Devin Booker's 23 points, list Grayson Allen (hamstring), Mark Williams (foot soreness), and Jordan Goodwin as questionable per latest reports, amplifying trader consensus on Thunder momentum amid Suns' bounce-back urgency.
